notes.src/civilization/simulation.js: Re-baselined in v13 for geography-driven district names, and again for biome 21: the two forest tests ([7,8,9,10,11]) had to learn the subtropical laurel forest, or a settlement standing in one would read its hinterland as treeless. Locked by the settlementFingerprint assertion in tests/onemap.test.mjs. Re-baselined again for state formation, deliberately this time. The administration step cost now treats mountain walls and river fords as real barriers rather than a mild surcharge, so a frontier falls on something you can point at; each founding council draws its reach from a long tail before the land search rather than after, so realms range from one province to forty-six instead of all being middling; and nameRealms() names a realm for the legend, landform, volcano or plate it holds rather than for its capital. physicalFingerprint and settlementFingerprint are unchanged and still asserted; politicalFingerprint moves because the borders themselves are the change.
notes.src/world/geography.js: Re-baselined three times. (a) Legendary places: nameLegends() writes only w.legends. (b) Two landform priors — irregular basin depressions and collision-belt plateaus. (c) Biomes 21 and 22, the subtropics: every humid cell from 7 to 21 C used to be called temperate, so a laurel forest at 19 C and a beech wood at 11 C carried the same two words and grew the same tree. Appended, never inserted, because the indices below are written into saves and into every biome test here. (b) and (c) move the world by design: physicalFingerprint dfd91476 -> 4b02963c -> 440ae5d0, settlementFingerprint 77c3b21f -> 73c1127f -> 6b6c5ea8, all asserted at the current values in tests/onemap.test.mjs and tests/climate.test.mjs.
notes.src/render/world-renderer.js: Re-baselined for two deliberate rendering changes. (a) Map clarity: supersampled backing store in resize(), Geometry.smoothTri() for per-vertex terrain normals and colours, buildLegends() markers. (b) Political layers: realms and diplomacy no longer paint a country's territory at all. Every border already carries a cased frontier line, and that is the whole of the country on this map; only the realm you have selected takes a faint wash, so the selection is answerable. Faiths, peoples, wealth and magic keep their full colour, where the colour is the measurement. Terrain vertex positions are untouched: the surface is locked by AtlasSpace.surface parity and the shared-edge check in tests/continuous.test.mjs, and the political palette by the coverage assertion in tests/onemap.test.mjs. The v12 shader and layer-visibility normalisations are folded into this baseline. Re-baselined again for the climate pass: buildSymbols() draws climate-driven vegetation (seven forms from CityEnvironment.canopy, with a treeline) via the shared plantForm() helper. Terrain, rivers, ice, dunes, volcanoes, camera, picking, legends and the shadow pipeline are unchanged. Also carries the two subtropical tree silhouettes, laurel and hardleaf, added with biomes 21 and 22. Two further rendering changes: the volcano symbol is gone — a vent's cone is already in w.height, so it drew a second schematic cone on top of the real mountain — and plantForm takes a coarse detail flag for the scatter that fills a whole visible landscape. Re-baselined again for Geometry.tri, which is now allocation-free: it had been building seven throwaway arrays and four spreads per triangle, about 3.6M allocations for a single town, and that was most of the wait after clicking into one. The arithmetic is unchanged down to the use of Math.hypot, so every vertex is bit-identical and the geometry-hash assertions across the suite pass untouched, which is what pins it. The city coherence fix enables slope-scaled polygon offset only during the shadow depth pass, removing diagonal self-shadow stripes on close terrain. Terrain geometry and physical simulation remain unchanged.
